implemented.summary: Pagurus is an optional API client; Conchbase owns execution, identity, task state, durable work, secrets, and permissions.
The paired 1.0.0 control client implements Agent management, configuration, task history, work control, capability records, and a write-only SecretHandle editor over published routes.
Every final surface checks its published Runtime capability, and every write uses an accepted typed client route.
One-shot SecretHandle values are cleared after submission; the client never receives, displays, stores, or resolves plaintext.
Seven labeled hash-based workspaces group the existing implemented surfaces without changing the published Runtime contract.
The Organization Console product and delivery direction is accepted as a paired long-range target, not implemented behavior.
Pagurus ADR 0017 accepts the paired typed-client and authority boundary for Conchbase's accepted but unimplemented 1.1.0 organization contract; no connected UI is implemented.

validationEvidence.summary: Pagurus runs npm run check, npm test, and npm run build in CI.
Conchbase's executable opt-in paired test dynamically imports published Pagurus clients over deterministic live loopback HTTP.
A completed 54-request same-origin proxy walkthrough is documented as validation evidence, not as an executable Pagurus repository fixture.
An executable jsdom/CSS fixture covers skip-link focus, keyboard navigation, active state, visible focus, reduced motion, and narrow/wide responsive rules.
An executable local fixture aligns typed-client paths, methods, and response envelopes with the paired Conchbase 47-path OpenAPI when the sibling checkout is present.

blockedDirections.summary: Tool request/approval presentation and decisions require a real Conchbase execution authorization contract and a paired Pagurus ADR.
Topology-neutral visual composition editing requires its own accepted client ADR and must not hardcode a canonical topology.
Install/enable/grant workflows, MCP servers, Skills, plugins, and process lifecycle require Runtime lifecycle and isolation contracts.
Remote runtime discovery, production pairing UX, desktop packaging, and cloud deployment require separate accepted contracts.
Generated client types require a separately accepted stable schema contract; current typed clients mirror the published OpenAPI explicitly.
OS keychain custody and replayable encrypted-at-rest values require a new Conchbase security ADR and a paired client boundary.
Single-entry primary conversation, attention-first project supervision, worker/delegation inspection, reports, and archive browsing over published organization contracts.

nextBoundedSlices.summary: Prepare non-authoritative client design and fixtures for the Organization Console without connected routes or a second schema.

invariants: Use only published Runtime API routes and keep response validation at the typed-client boundary.
Never read or write Conchbase private files or database.
Never store provider/tool credentials, SecretHandle plaintext, or runtime state in browser storage, bundles, URLs, logs, or errors.
Gate every final surface on its published Runtime capability.
Do not create a second Agent, task, work, configuration, or SecretHandle schema.
Distinguish implemented behavior from roadmap and validation evidence.
